entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The applicant has filed this SECOND bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail.

Applicant has been arrested on 22.12.2022 in connection with Crime No.514/2022 by Police Station Parasiya, District Chhindwara for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 466, 468, 471 and 34 of IPC.
2.
It is the submission of learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is suffering confinement since 22.12.2022 and charge sheet has already been filed.
Since the matter pertains to documentary evidence, therefore, chance of tampering with evidence/witnesses is remote.
Co-accused Vinod Singh has been given benefit of bail vide order dated 10.01.2023 in M.Cr.C. No.513/2023.

Even otherwise, it was other stakeholders in the Tehsil office, who were instrumental in preparation of documents in which Grandfather of applicant Ganesh Singh left 20 shares of Reliance Industry and Abhishek Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165622709/

entities.text: Abhishek Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 his father wanted to get benefits/dividends through transfer of shares in his name.
No pecuniary loss has been caused to anyone.
Confinement amounts to pre-trial detention.
Applicant does not bear any criminal record.
He seeks parity vis-a-vis order dated 10.01.2023 in M.Cr.C. No.513/2023 in respect of co-accused Vinod Singh.
The applicant undertakes to cooperate in trial/investigation.
Under these grounds, counsel prayed for bail.
3. Learned counsel for the respondent/State opposed the prayer and prayed for its dismissal.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the case diary.
5.
Considering the above submissions advanced by the learned counsel for the parties, but without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

It is hereby directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of trial Court.
